current.text: Curry has runner's knee. He has said publicly that the knee issue is a new normal.
His knee is the experts' main worry this season. Josh thinks the knee problem is getting worse, and Dan expects he could miss 30 games.
When he plays, experts see him as a top 10 to top 12 per game player in category leagues. He is still one of the best players in the league at age 38.
In recent expert mock drafts he went between pick 18 and pick 23. In one auction mock he went for 26 USD.
The newest expert calls say not to take him around pick 23 because of his knee and the bad Warriors team. Josh values him at about 40 USD per game but would not pay more than 25 USD.
The Warriors are seen as a bad team this season. Experts worry they could cut his minutes and rest veterans to protect their lottery odds.
He is the only player on the Warriors who really creates his own shot, so he is expected to carry a huge offensive load.
The Warriors have 15 back-to-backs, tied for second most. Their schedule is good for fantasy playoffs that end March 28.

durable.text: He is worth much more in category leagues than in points leagues.
He is an elite three-point shooter, with steady volume of more than 4 threes a game.
He is an elite free throw shooter at above 92 percent, and he is consistent at that level.
He gives strong points. His assists and steals are not special.
Turnovers are his weakest category for a guard.
Injury is the main fantasy risk with him. His runner's knee is a wear-and-tear issue, so expect maintenance rest days.

note: Healthy, Curry is a top 10 to 12 per game player in our format. He carries 3PM, FT% and PTS, and his only weak spot is turnovers, so he fits punt TO builds best. The price question is games played: he played 43 games last season, the knee is a new normal and the Warriors may rest veterans. Our league paid 42 USD for him last season, but Yahoo (31 USD) and ESPN (21 USD) are well below that and Josh would cap him at 25 USD, so bid in the 25 to 31 USD range and do not chase him to last year's price. Early in the season, watch how often he sits back-to-backs (the team has 15) and whether his minutes stay near 32. The schedule for our playoff weeks is good.
